In [[algebraic geometry]], the '''Koras&ndash;Russell cubic threefolds''' are smooth affine complex [[threefold]]s diffeomorphic to <math>\mathbf{C}^3</math>studied by {{harvtxt|Koras|Russell|1997}}. They have a hyperbolic action of a one-dimensional [[torus]] <math>\mathbf{C}^*</math>with a unique fixed point, such that the quotients of the threefold and the [[tangent space]] of the fixed point by this action are isomorphic. They were discovered in the process of proving the Linearization Conjecture in dimension 3. A linear action of <math>\mathbf{C}^*</math> on the affine space <math>\mathbf{A}^n</math> is one of the form <math>t*(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=(t^{a_1}x_1,t^{a_2}x_2,\ldots,t^{a_n}x_n)</math>, where <math>a_1,\ldots,a_n\in \mathbf{Z}</math> and <math>t\in\mathbf{C}^*</math>. The Linearization Conjecture in dimension <math>n</math> says that every algebraic action of <math>\mathbf{C}^*</math> on the complex affine space <math>\mathbf{A}^n</math> is linear in some algebraic coordinates on <math>\mathbf{A}^n</math>. M. Koras and P. Russell made a key step towards the solution in dimension 3, providing a list of threefolds (now called Koras-Russell threefolds) and proving <ref>{{cite journal|last1=Koras|first1=Mariusz|last2=Russell|first2=Peter|title=C<sup>∗</sup>-actions on C<sup>3</sup>: the smooth locus of the quotient is not of hyperbolic type|journal=J. Algebraic Geom.|date=1999|volume=8|issue=4|pages=603–694}}</ref> that the Linearization Conjecture for <math>n=3</math> holds if all those threefolds are [[exotic affine space|exotic affine 3-spaces]], that is, none of them is isomorphic to <math>\mathbf{A}^3</math>. This was later shown by Kaliman and Makar-Limanov using the [[ML-invariant]] of an [[affine variety]], which had been invented exactly for this purpose. 

Earlier than the above referred paper, Russell noticed that the hypersurface <math>R=\{x+x^2y+z^2+t^3=0\}</math> has properties very similar to the affine 3-space like contractibility and was interested in distinguishing them as [[Algebraic variety|algebraic varieties]]. This now follows from the computation that <math>ML(R)=\mathbf{C}[x]</math> and <math>ML(\mathbf{A}^3)=\mathbf{C}</math>.
